prompt: Find the average rate of change of $f(x) = x^2$ on the interval $[1, 3]$.
hint: Average rate of change is the slope of the line joining the two endpoints of the interval: rise over run.

hints.text: Average rate of change is the slope of the line joining the two endpoints of the interval: rise over run.
The endpoint values are $f(3) = 9$ and $f(1) = 1$, so the rise is $8$ and the run is $2$. Divide rise by run.
The slope is $\frac{8}{2} = 4$, so the average rate of change is $4$.

explanation: The average rate of change on $[a, b]$ is the secant slope $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$.
With endpoints $a = 1$ and $b = 3$ the slope formula becomes $\frac{f(3) - f(1)}{3 - 1} = \frac{9 - 1}{2}$.
The result is $4$. That is the slope of the secant line through $(1, 1)$ and $(3, 9)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why it is called a secant slope
steps: Plot $(1, 1)$ and $(3, 9)$ on the parabola and draw the straight line through them.
Its slope is $\frac{9 - 1}{3 - 1} = 4$ — ordinary Algebra 1 slope.
Later, sliding the second point toward the first turns this secant into a tangent, and the average rate into an instantaneous one.
